title: Kitchen Renovation Before and After Cost UK

blocks.text: Searching for kitchen renovation before and after cost examples can be more useful than looking at a single headline figure. As a rough guide, a simple refresh with the existing cabinets may cost several thousand pounds, while changing the layout, moving services or specifying bespoke cabinetry can take the same room into five-figure territory. This guide sets out illustrative UK examples so you can see what the money may pay for. Prices are rough guides rather than quotations: every project differs, and room size, access, condition, location and product choices all make a difference. Request a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.
What affects the cost of a kitchen transformation?

The biggest distinction is whether the renovation keeps the existing layout. Retaining the sink, cooker and major appliances can limit plumbing and electrical work, whereas moving them may involve new pipework, wiring, wall repairs and additional labour. Cabinet quality also matters: flat-pack units, rigid pre-assembled cabinets and bespoke furniture can have very different prices. Worktops range from laminate to timber, quartz and natural stone, with fabrication and fitting added to the material cost. Finally, the condition of the floor, walls and ceiling may only become clear once the old kitchen is removed.

blocks.text: Example 3: changing the layout and adding an island

Before: a narrow galley kitchen with limited worktop space, poor circulation and a sink positioned away from the main preparation area. After: the layout is opened up where possible, units are repositioned and a compact island or peninsula creates more storage and workspace. This is where before-and-after photographs can look most dramatic, but the cost is not just the extra cabinets. Moving water, waste, sockets, lighting and extraction may require more preparation, making the labour element higher than in a like-for-like replacement.

blocks.text: Example 4: higher-specification kitchen with structural work

Before: a small, enclosed kitchen that makes poor use of the available space. After: a larger connected kitchen-diner created by removing a non-load-bearing partition or making a carefully designed opening, with bespoke or premium cabinetry, durable worktops and upgraded appliances. If a wall is load-bearing, structural advice and approvals or inspections may be required depending on the work and location. Those costs are highly project-specific and should be confirmed before work starts. A project of this type may also overlap with wider house renovation work rather than being a standalone kitchen fitting job.

blocks.text: How to compare before-and-after quotes properly

Ask each contractor to separate products, labour and any third-party costs rather than providing one unexplained total. Check whether the quote includes removal, waste disposal, delivery, flooring, splashbacks, appliance connection, decorating, handles, panels and final sealant. Confirm whether VAT is included and whether the stated appliances are specific models or allowances. It is also sensible to keep a contingency for hidden defects and requested changes; some homeowners use around 10% as a planning allowance, although the appropriate amount depends on the property and the certainty of the design.
A practical way to control the budget

Decide early which changes matter most. If storage and appearance are the priority, retaining the layout may deliver better value. If the room is fundamentally awkward, spending more on plumbing and electrical alterations can improve everyday use for years. You can also balance the specification: invest in a hard-wearing worktop and well-planned storage, while choosing standard appliance sizes or a simpler splashback. faq.q: How much does a kitchen renovation cost in the UK?
faq.a: As a rough guide, a cosmetic refresh may cost around £5,000–£10,000, a complete mid-range replacement £12,000–£24,000, and a layout-changing project £18,000–£38,000 or more. Every project differs, so request a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to renovate a kitchen or replace it?
faq.a: Keeping sound cabinets and the existing layout is usually cheaper than a full replacement. However, damaged units, poor storage or unsuitable plumbing may make replacement better value over time.

faq.q: How much does moving a kitchen sink or cooker add?
faq.a: The cost depends on access, distances and the condition of the building. As a rough planning guide, moving a service may add around £500–£2,000, but every project differs and a site assessment is needed for a reliable figure. Request a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

faq.q: Do kitchen renovation quotes include appliances?
faq.a: Not always. Some quotes include named appliances, while others provide an allowance or cover connection only. Check the model, delivery, installation, disposal and VAT before comparing totals.

faq.q: How can I reduce the cost of a kitchen renovation?
faq.a: Retain the layout, choose standard cabinet sizes, compare worktop materials, limit structural changes and make the specification clear before ordering. Avoid cutting costs on essential electrical, plumbing and ventilation work.
